newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian T-bill prices stable, no strong rise seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian T-bill prices stable, no strong rise seen.

text.p: Prices of Russian government paper were barely changed on Monday from Friday's levels as record-low volumes of money were transfered for the trading, dealers said.
*Average yield rose to 20.13 pct from 18.97 pct on Friday
*Turnover fell to 4.37 trln rbls from 5.02 trln rbls
*Operators transferred 728 bln rbls - a record low volume since July 1, 1996
*Central Bank sold 238 bln rbls worth of T-bills
"The market showed a surprising stability," Raiffeisen Bank Austria dealer Alexander Losev said. "It was not even scared by such small sums and the lack of any real support from the central bank."
He said that since forward dollar rates were falling, dollar yields on bonds maturing in spring and summer 1998 were 12-14 percent annual, which was attractive for non-resident investors.

Bank Rossiisky Kredit dealer Konstantin Svyatny said widening spreads between hard currency yields on foreign and domestic debt would prompt foreign investors to increase their investment in domestic debt.

"Prices of our foreign debt (MinFin bonds) are rising very strongly and the spread of hard currency yields on foreign and domestic debt is growing, so I think non-residents can start investing money (into T-bills) again," Svyatny said.
Russian MinFins steadied above late Friday's levels following last week's rally in U.S. Treasuries amid confidence U.S interest rates would remain unchanged.
Dealers said banks would transfer more funds for trading on Tuesday but saw no significant price rise.
"We shall not see strong growth tomorrow, as everyone is scared by the strong buying seen on Friday," Rossiisky Natsionalny Kommerchesky Bank dealer Alexander Kuznetsov said.
Buying on Friday was spurred up by the Central Bank's decision to cut its refinancing rate to 24 percent from 36 percent from June 16.
